B0001.d: The restraint control module tests the firing loop of the first inflator stage in the driver airbag, which sits in the steering wheel hub and is fed through the clock spring. B0001 is stored when that loop is open, shorted or outside its resistance window; the fault byte added to the code names the exact type.
s: Airbag warning lamp or service airbag message stays on
Driver frontal airbag may not deploy in a crash
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed
c: Corroded or poorly seated connector between steering wheel harness and airbag module
Broken or worn conductor in the clock spring
Internal fault in the driver airbag module (stage 1 squib)
Chafed lead in the steering wheel or column harness

B0002.d: Dual-stage driver airbags hold a second charge that the restraint module fires only in severe crashes or after a short delay, so the cushion fills harder or for longer; a Nissan patent bases that choice on the change in vehicle speed and belt use. B0002 flags a fault in the firing loop of this second stage.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Driver airbag loses its second, high-severity stage
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed
c: Open stage 2 squib lead at the airbag module connector
Stage 2 track in the clock spring broken
Replacement restraint module loaded with unsuitable software (Land Rover SSM 74577)

B0003.d: Some driver airbag modules carry a third pyrotechnic element in addition to the two inflator stages, and B0003 covers its firing loop. FCA lists the code as driver frontal squib 3; its STAR case S2108000180 found B0003-2B (wires shorted together) next to B0001 and B0002 when connector locks behind the steering wheel were not engaged.
s: Airbag warning lamp on, often together with B0001 or B0002
Adaptive venting or third deployment stage unavailable
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed
c: Connector position assurance lock at the airbag module not engaged
Third squib or vent valve squib in the airbag module faulty
Damaged clock spring conductor for the third circuit

B0004.d: A knee airbag, also called an active knee bolster, sits in the lower dash below the steering column. It fills the space in front of the driver's knees and holds the lower body back in a frontal crash, mainly for unbelted occupants.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Driver knee airbag may not deploy in a frontal crash
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed
c: Faulty or loose knee airbag connector under the dash (Ford TSB 24-2444)
Harness pinched or damaged during work below the steering column
Internal fault in the knee airbag module

B0005.d: Some steering columns can change how much energy they soak up while collapsing in a frontal crash. In a Delphi/Nexteer patent a controller fires pyrotechnic actuators that force an absorber strap into a tighter path or couple in extra absorbers, matching the column to driver size and crash severity.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Adaptive energy absorption of the column unavailable, no effect on normal steering
Safety note: the column actuator is pyrotechnic; leave tests and connector work to a workshop with the battery disconnected
c: Restraint module configuration or software does not match the vehicle (Land Rover SSM 74577)
Open or shorted lead to the pyrotechnic column actuator
Faulty actuator in the steering column

B0006.d: B0006 is missing from the public J2012 code lists, which go straight from B0005 to B0010. The only documented use found has nothing to do with airbags: on the 2025 Ram 1500 the body control module stores B0006-11 for a short to ground in the latch control of the left RamBox stowage lid, fixed by a module update (flash 08-204-24).
s: Airbag warning lamp on when stored by the restraint module
On Ram 1500 2025 stowage lid will not open electrically, alarm may sound
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed
c: On Ram 1500 2025 the code belongs to the left stowage lid latch circuit of the body module, not the airbag
Driver airbag squib lead chafed against metal (ground short)
Insulation damage inside the clock spring

B0007.d: Like B0006, this number is absent from the public J2012 lists. FCA uses B0007-11 on the 2025 Ram 1500 for the latch control of the right RamBox stowage lid, again a short to ground in the body control module and cured by the same flash 08-204-24; an airbag meaning is not documented anywhere.
s: Airbag warning lamp on, affected stage disabled by the module
On Ram 1500 2025 right stowage lid inoperative
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed
c: On Ram 1500 2025 the code belongs to the right stowage lid latch circuit of the body module
Squib lead touching a powered wire in the column or steering wheel harness
Moisture bridging pins in a connector of the airbag circuit

B0010.d: The front passenger airbag in the dashboard is normally dual-stage like the driver bag, but it also depends on occupant detection: FMVSS 208 allows it to be suppressed for small occupants and requires a readiness indicator that monitors the system. B0010 reports a fault in the firing loop of its first stage.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Front passenger airbag may not deploy in a crash
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed
c: Loose, corroded or unlocked connector at the passenger airbag module
Harness damaged during dashboard or glovebox work
Internal fault in the passenger airbag module (stage 1 squib)

B0011.d: B0011 is the passenger counterpart of B0002: it concerns the second inflator stage of the dashboard airbag, which the module adds in severe crashes or fires with a delay. Mercedes-Benz logs B001113 for an open stage 2 squib of the front passenger airbag, and Mitsubishi lists B0011 as passenger airbag module 2.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Passenger airbag loses its second stage for severe crashes
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed
c: Poor contact on the stage 2 pins or open stage 2 lead
Stage 2 squib in the passenger airbag module faulty
Output stage in the restraint control module faulty

B0012.d: In the J2012 order B0012 is the third element of the front passenger airbag. Mercedes-Benz uses B001213 for the squib of the vent valve in that airbag, and Mitsubishi lists B0012 as passenger airbag module 3.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Depending on maker, passenger airbag venting or GM driver airbag stage 1 affected
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed
c: Open or shorted third squib (vent valve) in the passenger airbag (J2012 meaning)
On GM vehicles weak terminal tension or chafed wires at the steering wheel airbag coil

B0013.d: B0013 belongs to the knee airbag on the passenger side, which deploys from the lower glovebox area and keeps the passenger's knees and thighs from sliding under the dash. Mercedes-Benz logs B001313 for an open squib of the front passenger kneebag.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Passenger knee airbag (or on GM driver airbag stage 2) may not deploy
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed
c: Faulty connector at the passenger knee airbag (Ford TSB 24-2444)
On GM vehicles fault in the driver airbag stage 2 loop or clock spring
Internal fault in the passenger knee airbag

B0014.d: B0014 is not in the public J2012 code lists; there the driver knee airbag has B0004 and the passenger knee airbag B0013. The number is documented only at General Motors, and with another meaning.
s: Airbag warning lamp or service airbag message, often intermittent
Affected airbag may not deploy
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed
c: On GM vehicles loose or high-resistance side airbag connector under or in the driver seat
Seat harness chafed by seat frame, motor or foam
Internal fault in the airbag module served by this loop

B0015.d: B0015 does not appear in the public J2012 code lists, which assign the passenger knee airbag to B0013. Only General Motors documents the number, as the firing loop of the belt pretensioner built into the driver's retractor.
s: Airbag warning lamp on, sometimes intermittent
On GM, belt pretensioner may not fire; power seat may fail if the harness is shorted
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed
c: On GM vehicles loose or corroded connector at the driver belt pretensioner
Harness under the power seat rubbing on frame or seat motor (GM PIT4898C)
Internal fault in the pretensioner or airbag served by this loop

B0016.d: The public J2012 code lists skip B0016. General Motors used it in two generations with different meanings.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Passenger frontal airbag stage 1 (older GM) or left head airbag (later GM) may not deploy
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed
c: Squib leads shorted together or to ground in the passenger frontal loop (older GM)
Connector position assurance lock not seated (GM 08-09-41-002H)
On later GM vehicles fault in the left roof rail airbag loop

B0017.d: None of the public J2012 lists contains B0017 either. In older GM modules (Saab 9-5 2006, Saab 9-3 up to 2011) it marks an open passenger frontal stage 1 loop, set once the loop reads more than roughly 4.5 ohms for two seconds, so the component matches the title but the fault type does not.
s: Airbag warning lamp on or an OnStar SIR notification without lamp
Affected airbag stage may be disabled
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed
c: On GM 2020-22 models faulty SDM software, cured by reprogramming (21-NA-176)
Open passenger frontal stage 1 loop (older GM meaning)
Squib lead in contact with a powered wire

B0018.d: In the J2012 order of seating positions (driver, passenger, center, then second and third row) B0018 covers stage 1 of a frontal airbag for the middle seat of the first row. FMVSS 208 demands frontal airbags only for the outboard front seats, so such a bag is rare, and no carmaker publicly documents B0018 with this meaning.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Affected frontal airbag stage may not deploy
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed
c: Open or shorted stage 1 loop of a first-row center frontal airbag (J2012 meaning)
On older GM/Saab passenger frontal stage 1 loop shorted to battery or ground

B0019.d: B0019 is the stage 2 member of the first-row center frontal series B0018 to B001A, meant for the second inflator charge of a middle-seat frontal airbag. No carmaker publicly documents the code with this meaning.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
On GM the passenger frontal airbag stage 1 may not deploy
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed
c: On GM vehicles fretting corrosion in the passenger airbag in-line connector (HHR PI0117B)
Fault in the stage 2 loop of a first-row center frontal airbag (J2012 meaning)
Internal fault in the airbag module on this loop

B001A.d: B001A closes the first-row center frontal series and stands for a third stage of a middle-seat frontal airbag, matching B0003 for the driver and B0012 for the passenger. No carmaker documents it publicly in this sense.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
On GM the driver anchor pretensioner may not fire
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed
c: On GM vehicles pinched, misrouted or corroded anchor pretensioner harness
Fault in the third stage loop of a first-row center frontal airbag (J2012 meaning)

B0020.d: B0020 covers the firing loop of the left front side airbag, the thorax bag usually built into the outer flank of the driver seat backrest. Toyota names B002011 and B002012 as short to ground and short to battery on the 2022 Tundra, where the wireless phone charger caused false entries that new SRS software cures (TSB005722).
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Left front side airbag may not deploy in a side impact
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed
c: Poor contact or corrosion at the side airbag connector or jumper harness under or in the seat
Internal fault in the left seat side airbag module
Pinched or chafed side airbag lead in the seat frame
Restraint module software reacting to interference, e.g. Toyota Tundra 2022 with wireless charger

B0021.d: In the J2012 order B0021 is the first firing loop of the left curtain airbag, the bag that drops from the roof rail over the side windows. Mitsubishi files it under the left curtain module and stores byte 11, 12, 13 or a short to another circuit once the condition has lasted 2 seconds.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Left curtain airbag may not deploy in a side impact or rollover
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed
c: Raised contact resistance at the curtain airbag or restraint module connector
Damaged lead along the A-, B- or C-pillar or the roof rail
Internal fault in the left curtain airbag module
Fault or unsuitable software in the restraint control module

B0022.d: B0022 belongs to a second firing loop for the left curtain airbag. Mercedes-Benz shows what that means in practice: on the A-Class, CLA and GLB, B002213 is an open squib in the left rear window bag, the curtain section for the rear seats, while B0021 serves the front one (LI54.21-P-070658, version 1 of 2019 and version 4 of 2020).
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Head protection for the left rear seat may be missing
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed
c: Raised contact resistance at the restraint module connector (Mercedes LI54.21-P-070658)
Damaged lead to the rear curtain section at the C-pillar or roof rail
Internal fault in the rear left curtain airbag module
Fault or unsuitable software in the restraint control module

B0023.d: B0023 does not appear in the J2012 code lists, which jump from B0022 to B0028, and no carmaker documents it as a ground short of a left side airbag stage. It is documented at General Motors with another meaning: in the Saab 9-4X 2011 manual B0023 is the right roof rail (curtain) airbag loop, with bytes for short to battery (01), short to ground (02), open (04) and resistance above 4.2 or below 1.4 ohms (0D, 0E), each
s: Airbag warning lamp on
The airbag on the affected loop may not deploy
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed
c: Connector position assurance not engaged, so shorting bars bridge the loop (GM 08-09-41-002H)
Internal fault in the affected airbag module

B0024.d: B0024 is missing from the public J2012 lists; there the right front side airbag is B0028. General Motors used the number twice.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Depending on the vehicle, the driver airbag or a seat side airbag may be affected
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed
c: Restraint module software fault on 2021 GM models (PIT5827, 21-NA-176)
Short to ground or battery in the driver frontal stage 1 loop (older GM/Saab)
Worn clock spring in the driver airbag loop (older GM/Saab)

B0025.d: No public J2012 code list contains B0025, and no manufacturer publicly describes a second stage of a left side airbag under this number. The only trace is at General Motors: the Saab 9-4X 2011 manual groups B0025 with the roof rail airbag codes B0016 and B0023 but gives no descriptor for it.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Side or curtain protection may be reduced on the affected side
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed
c: Open, shorted or high-resistance squib loop of the airbag the module assigns to this code
Connector or its position lock not fully engaged
Fault or unsuitable software in the restraint control module

B0026.d: B0026 is missing from the public J2012 lists. General Motors documents it in older restraint modules with a meaning other than the title: on the 2006 Saab 9-5, B0026 is an open circuit in driver frontal stage 1, set when the measured resistance stays above 4.5 ohms, tolerance 0.2, for 2 seconds; the Saab 9-3 manuals add bytes for an open loop and too high resistance in the same driver circuit.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Depending on the vehicle, the driver airbag may not deploy
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed
c: Airbag connector or its position lock not fully seated (GM 08-09-41-002H)
Broken track in the clock spring (driver loop on older GM/Saab)
Open squib inside the airbag module

B0028.d: B0028 is the right-hand twin of B0020: the firing loop of the right front side airbag, normally in the outer flank of the passenger seat. Honda asked for parts from 2018-20 Accord and CR-V and from the 2015 TLX that stored B0028-13, an open or raised resistance in the passenger side airbag inflator.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Right front side airbag may not deploy in a side impact
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed
c: Poor contact or corrosion at the side airbag connector or jumper harness under or in the seat
Internal fault in the right seat side airbag inflator
Lead pinched or stretched by seat adjustment
Restraint module software reacting to interference (Toyota Tundra 2022)

B0029.d: B0029 stands for the first firing loop of the right curtain airbag. FCA's STAR case S2010000001 for the 2019 Ram heavy-duty pickup reads B0029-11 as a ground short in right curtain squib 1 and sends the technician to the wiring at the C-pillar trim fixings.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Right curtain airbag may not deploy in a side impact or rollover
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed
c: Lead pinched or chafed at pillar trim fixings (FCA S2010000001)
Raised contact resistance at the curtain or restraint module connector
Internal fault in the right curtain airbag module

B002A.d: B002A is the second firing loop of the right curtain airbag, needed only where the right side has two curtain inflators or a separate curtain section for the rear seats. Mercedes-Benz uses it that way on the A-Class, CLA and GLB: B002A13 marks an open squib in the right rear window bag, while the front part reports B0029; a known trigger was poor contact at the control unit plug (LI54.21-P-070658).
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Head protection for the right rear seat may be missing
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed
c: Raised contact resistance at the restraint module connector (Mercedes LI54.21-P-070658)
Damaged lead to the rear curtain section at the C-pillar or roof rail
Internal fault in the rear right curtain airbag module

B0030.d: In J2012 the B003x block covers the second seat row, and B0030 is the left rear side airbag, mounted in the rear door or the outer backrest. Mitsubishi files B0030 under the rear side airbag module LH and sets a short to another circuit after 2 seconds.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Rear left side airbag may not deploy in a side impact
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed
c: Raised contact resistance at the restraint module or rear side airbag connector
Damaged lead in the rear door transition or rear seat backrest
Internal fault in the rear left side airbag module

B0031.d: B0031 points to the first firing stage of a frontal airbag that protects the left rear passenger, so it can only be stored where such a bag exists. The known production case is Mercedes-Benz's S-Class of 2020: an optional rear airbag (standard on the Maybach) unfolds from the back of the front seat for the two outer rear seats, built as a gas-filled tube frame that draws ambient air into its cushion.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Left rear passenger may lose frontal airbag protection in a crash
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed
c: Loose or corroded connector of the airbag lead routed through the front seat backrest
Internal fault in the rear-seat airbag module in the front seatback
Lead stretched or pinched by the seat track or folding mechanism
Restraint module configured for equipment the vehicle does not have (wrong part or coding)

B0032.d: B0032 concerns a second igniter for the rear-seat frontal airbag on the left. A second stage lets the module add gas later or skip it, depending on crash severity and on who sits behind the seat; a Mercedes-Benz filing for a backrest-mounted rear airbag allows separate deployment devices for its chambers so they can fire in sequence.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Rear-seat airbag may inflate with less force or not at all
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed
c: Open or short only in the stage 2 pair of wires to the rear airbag
Loose or corroded connector of the airbag lead routed through the front seat backrest
Faulty second igniter inside the rear-seat airbag module
Restraint module configured for equipment the vehicle does not have (wrong part or coding)

B0033.d: B0033 is the third deployment element of a frontal airbag for the left second-row seat. A third igniter can be a further gas chamber; a Breed patent describes an inflator with one igniter per chamber whose firing order and 0 to 25 ms delays the controller chooses.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Adaptive inflation of the left rear airbag is lost
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed
c: Connector position assurance lock missing or not seated, so the plug works loose
Damaged stage 3 lead or igniter in the rear airbag
Restraint module configured for equipment the vehicle does not have (wrong part or coding)

B0034.d: B0034 is absent from the J2012 lists, which skip from B0033 to B0038 in the second-row block, and no carmaker or bulletin documents it publicly; the code cannot be traced to a real vehicle. The title describes a second firing stage for the right side airbag.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Right side airbag protection may be reduced
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed
c: Fault in the squib loop the module assigns to this code
Poor contact or corrosion at the side airbag connector or jumper harness under or in the seat
Fault or unsuitable software in the restraint control module

B0036.d: B0036 appears neither in the public J2012 lists nor in any accessible manufacturer document, so the code is not publicly verifiable. Its title describes a short to ground in a second stage of the right side airbag.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Right side airbag may not deploy in a side impact
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed
c: Chafed side airbag lead touching the seat frame or body
Connector lock not engaged, shorting bars bridge the loop
Internal short in the side airbag module

B0038.d: B0038 watches the firing loop of the side airbag for the right-hand second-row seat, fitted in the rear door trim or in the outer bolster of the rear backrest. Mitsubishi lists it as rear side airbag module RH with exactly this J2012 wording and logs B0038-12 when the circuit has been shorted to supply for 2 seconds.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Right rear passenger may lack side airbag protection
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed
c: Poor contact at the rear side airbag connector in the door or rear seat
Internal fault in the right rear side airbag module
Lead chafed against a powered wire, e.g. at the rear seat fold or B-pillar

B0039.d: B0039 belongs to the right-hand rear-seat frontal airbag, stage 1, which is the primary charge that the module fires in any frontal crash severe enough to need the bag. The bag sits in the back of the passenger seat ahead; Mercedes-Benz offers this layout as an S-Class option and fits it as standard to the Maybach, where it is meant to ease head and neck loads on belted outer rear passengers.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Right rear passenger may lose frontal airbag protection
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed
c: Loose or corroded connector of the airbag lead routed through the front seat backrest
Internal fault in the right rear-seat airbag module
Lead stretched or pinched by the seat track or folding mechanism
Restraint module configured for equipment the vehicle does not have (wrong part or coding)

B003A.d: B003A covers stage 2 of the right rear-seat frontal airbag. The second charge allows the module to soften or strengthen inflation; for a rear bag this matters because the person behind the front seat may be an adult, a child or a child seat facing either way, a point Mercedes-Benz stressed when it introduced the S-Class rear airbag in 2020.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Rear airbag may not adapt its inflation to the occupant
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed
c: Open or short only in the stage 2 pair of wires
Loose or corroded connector of the airbag lead routed through the front seat backrest
Faulty second igniter in the right rear-seat airbag
Restraint module configured for equipment the vehicle does not have (wrong part or coding)

B003B.d: B003B is the third firing element of the right rear-seat frontal airbag. In front airbags Mercedes-Benz uses this third position for the squib that opens a vent valve and lets gas escape (B000313 driver, B001213 passenger); a patent from Breed shows the other option, a third gas chamber with its own igniter that the controller can fire later, for example in a second impact.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Right rear airbag may deploy without its adaptive third stage
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed
c: Damaged stage 3 lead or vent squib in the right rear airbag
Loose or corroded connector of the airbag lead routed through the front seat backrest
Restraint module configured for equipment the vehicle does not have (wrong part or coding)

B0040.d: B0040 is reserved for a side airbag at the left seat of a third row, as found in some seven-seat SUVs and vans; most of them protect that row only with an extended curtain. A Joyson (TK Holdings) patent states its seatback side module may serve any row, third included, and a GM application gives rear-row side bags their own gas generators and allows the rear row to be the third.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Left third-row occupant may lack side airbag protection
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed
c: Poor contact at the side airbag connector of the third-row seat or rear quarter trim
Lead strained by folding or removing the third-row seat
Internal fault in the third-row side airbag

B0041.d: B0041 would report the first stage of a frontal airbag for the left third-row seat, which would have to deploy from the back of the second-row seat in front of it. Such bags are described in patents, for instance a Daimler application for an airbag at the rear of a front seat and a Mercedes-Benz filing that compensates for a sliding seat with stacked chambers, but no production vehicle with third-row frontal airbags
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Frontal airbag for the left third-row seat may not deploy
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed
c: Loose connector of the airbag lead in the second-row seatback
Lead strained when the second-row seat is folded or slid
Restraint module configured for equipment the vehicle does not have (wrong part or coding)

B0042.d: B0042 stands for the second stage of a frontal airbag aimed at the left third-row passenger. A second stage only makes sense with an inflator that has two independently fired charges, as in Breed's multi-chamber design where the controller picks which chamber fires first and the gap between them.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Adaptive two-stage inflation for this seat is unavailable
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed
c: Open or short only in the stage 2 wiring
Connector lock not engaged at the airbag plug
Restraint module configured for equipment the vehicle does not have (wrong part or coding)

B0043.d: B0043 completes the left third-row frontal group as its stage 3 element. By analogy with front airbags this can be a vent valve squib, as Mercedes-Benz uses for B000313 and B001213, or a further gas chamber like the third chamber in Breed's patent that is kept for a second collision.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Third deployment element of this airbag is disabled
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed
c: Short between two firing loops in a shared harness
Restraint module configured for equipment the vehicle does not have (wrong part or coding)

B0046.d: B0046 appears in none of the accessible J2012 code lists, which jump from B0043 to B0048, and no carmaker or bulletin uses it publicly, so the code cannot be traced to a vehicle. Its title describes an open firing loop of the left curtain airbag that drops from the roof rail.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Left curtain airbag may not deploy in a side impact or rollover
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed
c: Unplugged or loose curtain airbag connector at the pillar or roof rail
Broken lead in the roof rail harness, e.g. after headliner work
Open igniter inside the left curtain airbag

B0047.d: B0047 is missing from the accessible J2012 lists as well, and no vehicle maker or NHTSA bulletin documents it, so it is not publicly traceable. The title names a grounded left curtain airbag loop; this inflatable curtain covers the side windows in side impacts and rollovers.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Left curtain airbag deployment may be blocked
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed
c: Insulation of the curtain lead chafed through against the body
Lead pinched by a pillar trim or headliner clip
Internal short to housing in the left curtain airbag

B0048.d: B0048 is the right-hand counterpart of B0040: the deployment loop of a side airbag for the right seat in a third row. Few vehicles have one, because the third row usually relies on a curtain that reaches back to the D-pillar.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Right third-row occupant may lack side airbag protection
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed
c: Poor contact at the third-row right side airbag connector
Lead damaged by folding, sliding or removing the third-row seat
Restraint module configured for equipment the vehicle does not have (wrong part or coding)

B0049.d: B0049 marks the stage 1 charge of a right third-row frontal bag, the main charge of a bag that would have to come out of the second-row seatback ahead of it. Daimler's application for a bag mounted behind a front seat and Mercedes-Benz's later design with chambers that bridge a changing seat gap show how such a bag can be built; in series, Mercedes offers rear frontal airbags only for the outer second-row seats of it
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Frontal airbag for the right third-row seat may not deploy
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed
c: Restraint module configured for equipment the vehicle does not have (wrong part or coding)
Loose connector of the airbag lead in the second-row seatback
Lead strained when the second-row seat is folded or slid

B004A.d: B004A is the second-stage loop of the right third-row frontal airbag. Stage 2 is a separately ignited charge: Breed's patent shows an inflator whose chambers each carry their own igniter, fired alone, together or with a delay chosen by the controller, and Mercedes-Benz's rear airbag filing allows one deployment device per chamber for sequential filling.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Two-stage inflation for the right third-row seat is lost
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed
c: Open or short only in the stage 2 wiring
Loose connector in the second-row seatback
Restraint module configured for equipment the vehicle does not have (wrong part or coding)

B004B.d: B004B is the last code of the third-row frontal block: stage 3 of the right-hand bag. What a third element does is up to the maker.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Right third-row airbag may deploy without its third element
Safety note: do not probe the airbag circuit yourself; unplug airbag connectors only with the battery disconnected and the stated wait time observed
c: Restraint module configured for equipment the vehicle does not have (wrong part or coding)
Loose connector in the second-row seatback

B0050.d: B0050 monitors the switch in the driver's belt buckle that tells the restraint module whether the belt is latched; the module uses it for the belt reminder and for choosing the airbag and pretensioner response. Usually a two-wire Hall sensor whose current changes when the steel tongue enters the buckle.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Belt reminder for the driver may warn wrongly or stay silent
Restraint module may treat the driver as unbelted and adapt airbag and pretensioner firing
Safety note: the buckle connector sits under the seat next to the side airbag and pretensioner plugs; disconnect the battery and observe the wait time before unplugging anything
c: Corroded terminals at the inline connector between buckle and seat harness
Faulty Hall sensor or switch inside the driver buckle
Buckle lead pinched or stretched by the seat track
Foreign object or debris in the buckle confusing the sensor

B0051.d: B0051 belongs to the buckle sensor of a middle seat in the front row, found in pickups and vans with a front bench for three. FMVSS 208 requires a belt warning only for the outboard front seats, so a centre buckle sensor is extra equipment that feeds the restraint module and, where fitted, a reminder for that place.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Centre seat belt reminder may be wrong or missing
Safety note: the buckle connector sits under the seat next to the side airbag and pretensioner plugs; disconnect the battery and observe the wait time before unplugging anything
c: Loose or corroded connector of the centre buckle under the bench seat
Faulty Hall switch in the centre buckle
Lead strained by a fold-down centre seat or console

B0052.d: B0052 concerns the front passenger's buckle sensor, reporting to the airbag module whether the tongue is latched. That signal feeds the passenger belt reminder that FMVSS 208 requires at the front outboard seats and helps the module decide how the passenger airbag and pretensioner fire.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Passenger belt reminder warns although the belt is fastened, or stays silent
Passenger airbag and pretensioner strategy may assume an unbelted occupant
Safety note: the buckle plug sits under the seat next to airbag and pretensioner plugs; only unplug it with the battery disconnected and the wait time observed
c: Loose or corroded buckle connector under the passenger seat
Faulty Hall sensor inside the passenger buckle
Buckle lead pinched or torn by the seat rails or a mat fixing
Input fault inside the airbag control module

B0053.d: B0053 is the J2012 slot for the buckle sensor at the second row's left seat. Rear buckle sensors drive the rear belt reminder: for vehicles built from September 2028, FMVSS 208 S7.5(c) demands a start-up display of which rear belts are fastened or open and a warning when one is unlatched while driving.
s: Airbag or rear belt warning lamp on
Rear belt display shows the left seat wrongly as fastened or unfastened
Safety note: the buckle plug sits under the seat near pretensioner and side airbag plugs; only unplug it with the battery disconnected and the wait time observed
c: Loose or corroded buckle connector under the left rear seat
Faulty switch or Hall sensor in the left rear buckle
Lead damaged by folding or sliding the second-row seat
Older GM/Saab module: deployment record with a loop fault, module replacement needed

B0054.d: B0054 is reserved for the buckle sensor of the middle seat in the second row. That position often has its buckle in a split bench or under a fold-down armrest, so the lead runs through moving seat parts.
s: Airbag or rear belt warning lamp on
Middle rear seat shown wrongly in the belt status display
Safety note: buckle plugs under the rear bench lie close to pretensioner wiring; only unplug them with the battery disconnected and the wait time observed
c: Lead of the centre buckle strained at the split bench or armrest hinge
Loose or corroded connector of the centre buckle
Faulty Hall switch in the centre buckle

B0055.d: B0055 stands for the buckle sensor of the right seat in the second row, behind the front passenger and in vans often beside the sliding door. Where that seat is a removable captain's chair, a disconnect in the buckle lead is unavoidable; IEE points out in a patent that a wireless buckle sensor alone cannot tell the module whether the seat is fitted, so a missing signal may mean a fault or simply an empty floor.
s: Airbag or rear belt warning lamp on
Right rear seat shown wrongly or missing in the belt status display
Safety note: seat and buckle plugs under the seat lie near pretensioner and side airbag lines; only unplug them with the battery disconnected and the wait time observed
c: Seat connector not engaged after the removable seat was refitted
Corroded buckle connector, e.g. from wet floor near the sliding door
Faulty sensor in the right rear buckle

B0056.d: B0056 belongs to the left third-row seat's buckle sensor, found in larger SUVs, minivans and seven-seat estates. Third-row seats usually fold flat into the floor, so the buckle lead has to pass through the folding mechanism and is flexed every time the cargo area is extended.
s: Airbag or rear belt warning lamp on
Fault may appear only with the third-row seat folded or raised
Safety note: third-row buckle plugs can sit near pretensioner wiring; only unplug them with the battery disconnected and the wait time observed
c: Buckle lead broken or chafed in the fold-flat mechanism of the third row
Loose or corroded connector at the third-row seat
Faulty sensor in the left third-row buckle

B0057.d: In J2012, B0057 is the buckle sensor for the third row's centre seat, a position found only in eight-seat vans and SUVs. FMVSS 208 S7.5(c) will require a belt warning there from September 2028.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Depending on the module: wrong belt status for the middle third-row seat, or passenger pretensioner possibly inactive
Safety note: buckle and pretensioner plugs carry firing circuits nearby; only unplug them with the battery disconnected and the wait time observed
c: Faulty buckle sensor or lead at the middle third-row seat
Older GM trucks: broken wire in the rear door harness to the pretensioner (bulletin 14609)
Older GM/Saab module: shorted passenger pretensioner squib or connector

B0058.d: B0058 is the J2012 code for the buckle sensor at the right seat of the third row. The sensor reports a latched or free belt to the module that runs the rear belt display, which FMVSS 208 S7.5(c) makes mandatory for every rear seat from September 2028.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Depending on the module: right third-row seat shown wrongly, or passenger pretensioner may not fire
Safety note: buckle and pretensioner plugs carry firing circuits nearby; only unplug them with the battery disconnected and the wait time observed
c: Buckle lead of the right third-row seat damaged by folding or loading
Older GM/Saab module: open passenger pretensioner loop, e.g. broken rear door wire
Faulty sensor in the right third-row buckle

B0060.d: B0060 refers to a belt tension sensor in the driver's belt, a force gauge usually bolted to the lower anchor with the webbing running through it. In Delphi's design a spring-loaded slider moves against the belt pull and a Hall element between two magnets turns the travel into a voltage; the springs give way at roughly 5 to 15 lb.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Restraint module may fall back to a default firing strategy for the driver
Safety note: the sensor plug sits beside the seat near pretensioner and side airbag plugs; only unplug it with the battery disconnected and the wait time observed
c: Loose or corroded connector at the anchor-mounted tension sensor
Tension sensor output stuck or out of range, e.g. jammed slider
Sensor lead pinched under the seat or at the sill trim

B0061.d: B0061 covers the belt tension sensor of the front passenger seat, a key input for passenger occupant classification. FMVSS 208 lets carmakers meet the child-seat rules for advanced airbags by fitting a system that automatically switches the passenger airbag off for small occupants.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Passenger airbag status indicator may show an unexpected on or off state
A tightly fastened child seat may not be recognised reliably
Safety note: the sensor plug sits beside the passenger seat near airbag and pretensioner plugs; only unplug it with the battery disconnected and the wait time observed
c: Loose or corroded plug at the passenger belt tension sensor
Tension sensor reading out of range or stuck
Input fault in the occupant classification or airbag module

B0062.d: None of the publicly available J2012 code lists contain B0062; they jump from B0061 to B0070, and no carmaker describes it with the knee airbag meaning shown in the title. J2012 files knee airbag loops under B0004 for the driver and B0013 for the passenger, with the fault type in the added byte; Mercedes-Benz logs kneebag squib faults as B000413 and B001313, and in that scheme a grounded loop would carry byte 11 inst
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Knee airbag may stay inactive in a frontal crash
Safety note: knee airbag plugs sit under the dashboard; do not probe the circuit and only unplug them with the battery disconnected and the wait time observed
c: Knee airbag lead chafed against a dash bracket or steering column part
Damaged knee airbag connector after work under the dashboard
Saab 9-3: fault in the driver-side curtain or rollover bar loop instead

B0064.d: No publicly available J2012 code list includes B0064; there, B0060 names the driver belt tension sensor. Older airbag modules from General Motors do use it: on the 2006 Saab 9-5, B0064 is set when the resistance of the driver pretensioner loop stays below 1.5 ohms, with a 0.2-ohm tolerance, for 2 seconds; B0065 marks an interrupted loop and B0066 a voltage at pin 34 outside 1.0 to 4.1 V.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Driver belt pretensioner may not work properly in a crash
Safety note: pretensioner plugs sit at the B-pillar or under the seat; do not probe the loop and only unplug them with the battery disconnected and the wait time observed
c: Pretensioner leads shorted together, e.g. squashed harness at the B-pillar
Colorado/Canyon extended cab: fatigued wires in the rear door harness (bulletin 14609)
Internal fault of the driver pretensioner squib

B0070.d: B0070 covers the firing loop of the driver's first (A) belt pretensioner, the squib the airbag module ignites to take slack out of the belt in a crash. A short or open in that loop lets the module no longer count on the device, so it lights the airbag lamp.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Driver belt is not tightened in a crash; airbags themselves are usually unaffected
Safety note: the pretensioner is a pyrotechnic part; work on it only with the battery disconnected and the wait time observed, ideally at a specialist workshop
c: Loose or corroded plug at the driver pretensioner (B-pillar base or seat side)
Firing lead chafed by seat rails or trim clips
Interference from added electronics, e.g. a wireless charger (Toyota Tundra 2022, ECU update)
Internal fault in the pretensioner squib

B0071.d: B0071 is reserved for a pretensioner at the middle seat of the first row, which exists only where a three-person front bench is fitted. The airbag module would watch this squib like any other firing loop and flag an open, a short or a resistance outside its window.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Middle front occupant gets no belt pretensioning in a crash
Safety note: pyrotechnic component; disconnect the battery, wait the specified time and leave the work to a specialist workshop
c: Plug under the front bench centre seat loose or corroded
Harness damaged when the centre seat or console is folded or removed
Airbag module configured for a centre pretensioner the vehicle does not have
Internal fault of the centre pretensioner

B0072.d: B0072 reports a fault in the deployment loop of the front passenger's A-stage belt pretensioner. While that loop is faulty the device cannot be relied on to fire, so the airbag module lights its lamp and keeps the code.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Front passenger belt may stay slack in a crash
Safety note: the pretensioner is pyrotechnic; only handle it de-energised (battery off, wait time) and have it serviced at a specialist workshop
c: Passenger pretensioner plug not latched or corroded
Lead pinched at the passenger seat base or B-pillar trim
Interference from added electronics such as a wireless charger

B0073.d: B0073 concerns the pretensioner at the left outer seat of the second row, normally built into the rear retractor. Mitsubishi documents it under exactly this name: with the ignition on, its airbag sensor unit stores B0073 with byte 11, 12, 13, 1A or 1B for a short to ground, a short to power, an open, lines shorted to each other or excessive resistance, and with byte 55 when the stored configuration does not match the
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Left rear occupant gets no belt pretensioning in a crash
Safety note: pyrotechnic part in the rear retractor; work only with the system de-energised and preferably at a specialist workshop
c: Plug at the left rear retractor loose or damaged after trim or seat removal
Harness to the left rear pretensioner shorted to ground or power
Airbag module configuration does not match the fitted rear pretensioners (Mitsubishi byte 55)
Internal fault of the left rear pretensioner or of the airbag module

B0074.d: B0074 would flag the firing loop of a pretensioner at the second row's middle seat. Rear centre belts with their own pretensioner are rare; IIHS rear-seat tests concentrate on the outboard positions, and no carmaker publishes B0074 with the J2012 meaning.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
On GM vehicles also passenger airbag status shows OFF with an adult seated
Safety note: restraint parts may be pyrotechnic or part of the airbag control; disconnect the battery, observe the wait time and use a specialist workshop
c: On GM vehicles, fault in the passenger presence sensor mat or its pinched wire (older GM meaning)
Plug of the rear centre pretensioner disturbed when the bench is folded or removed
Open or short in the harness to the rear centre seat

B0075.d: B0075 is the right-hand counterpart of B0073: the pretensioner at the second row's right outer seat. Mitsubishi lists it as PRE-TEN REAR RH with the J2012 title and tests the circuit whenever the ignition is on; byte 11 stands for a short to ground and 13 for an open circuit, while further bytes cover shorts to power, crossed wires, high resistance or a configuration mismatch, each after 2 seconds.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Right rear occupant without belt pretensioning in a crash
Safety note: the rear retractor contains a pyrotechnic charge; work on it only de-energised and leave it to a specialist workshop
c: Plug at the right rear retractor not fully latched after interior work
Chafed lead to the right rear pretensioner (short to ground or power)
Interference from added electronics, fixed by an ECU update (Toyota Tundra 2022)
Internal fault of the right rear pretensioner

B0076.d: B0076 belongs to the pretensioner at the left seat of the third row, a position found only in vehicles with a third seat row. No carmaker publishes B0076 with this meaning.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Third-row left occupant without pretensioning in a crash
Safety note: pyrotechnic belt component; disconnect the battery and wait before touching it, repair at a specialist workshop
c: Plug at the third-row left belt disturbed by folding or removing the seat
Harness damaged by luggage or trim work in the cargo area
Airbag module coded for a third-row pretensioner that is not fitted

B0077.d: B0077 stands for the pretensioner at the middle seat of the third row. Hardly any vehicle fits one, and no manufacturer documents B0077 with this J2012 meaning; Mercedes, which equips some models with third-row tensioning retractors, lists only a left and a right unit (B00E7/B00E6).
s: Airbag warning lamp on
On Saab, side airbag deployment on the driver side may be impaired
Safety note: airbag sensors and pretensioners belong to the pyrotechnic restraint system; work only de-energised and at a specialist workshop
c: On older Saab 9-3/9-5, fault at the driver-side side-impact or B-pillar sensor (older GM meaning)
Plug of the third-row centre pretensioner disturbed during seat folding or removal
Airbag module coded for a centre pretensioner that is not installed

B0078.d: B0078 refers to the right seat of the third row and its belt pretensioner. No carmaker publishes B0078 in this J2012 sense, and Mercedes models with third-row tensioning retractors log the right-hand unit as B00E6 instead.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Third-row right occupant without pretensioning, or on Saab impaired side-impact detection on the passenger side
Safety note: pyrotechnic restraint parts; only work on them with the battery disconnected, after the wait time, at a specialist workshop
c: On older Saab 9-3/9-5, fault at the passenger-side side-impact or B-pillar sensor (older GM meaning)
Plug at the third-row right belt loosened when the seat was folded or removed
Internal fault of the third-row right pretensioner

B0079.d: B0079 marks the driver's second (B) pretensioner. Mercedes-Benz uses the code in exactly this way: in LI54.21-P-070658, valid for A-Class, CLA and GLB, B007913 is an open circuit in the squib of the belt end fitting tensioner on the driver's side, while the retractor of the same seat appears as B007E.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Driver's lap belt section not tightened in a crash
Safety note: the end fitting tensioner is pyrotechnic; never probe it live – battery off, wait time, specialist workshop
c: Plug at the driver's belt end fitting tensioner beside the seat loose or corroded
Lead to the end fitting tensioner pinched by the seat rail
On a 2006 Saab 9-5, wrong side-impact sensor fitted (older GM meaning)
Internal fault of the end fitting tensioner squib

B007A.d: B007A is the passenger-side twin of B0079 and covers the second pretensioner on the front passenger seat. Mercedes lists B007A13 for an open in the squib of the passenger's belt end fitting tensioner on the A-, CLA- and GLB-Class and keeps the passenger retractor apart as B007F.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Passenger's lap belt not tightened in a crash, higher risk of sliding under it
Safety note: pyrotechnic tensioner next to the seat; disconnect the battery, observe the wait time, have a specialist workshop do the repair
c: Plug at the passenger end fitting tensioner disturbed, e.g. after seat removal
Lead to the lap tensioner pinched under the passenger seat
Internal fault of the passenger lap tensioner

B007B.d: B007B would cover a second pretensioner on the outboard left seat in row two, for example a lap tensioner in addition to the retractor unit. No manufacturer publishes B007B.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Left rear lap belt not tightened in a crash
Safety note: pyrotechnic part at the rear seat; work only de-energised (battery off, wait) and at a specialist workshop
c: Plug of the left rear lap or anchor tensioner disturbed when the bench was removed
Airbag module coded for a rear B-stage tensioner that is not fitted
Floor harness to the left rear seat damaged

B007C.d: B007C is the second-row right counterpart of B007B: an additional pretensioner stage at the right outer rear seat. No manufacturer publishes this code.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Right rear lap belt not pretensioned in a crash
Safety note: the tensioner contains a pyrotechnic charge; only work on it with the battery disconnected and at a specialist workshop
c: Plug of the right rear buckle or anchor tensioner loosened during seat work
Airbag module configuration lists a stage that is not installed
Internal fault of the right rear B-stage tensioner

B007D.d: B007D names a second pretensioner at the middle seat of the second row. No carmaker documents it, and since even one pretensioner at the rear centre seat is uncommon, a second stage there is rarer still.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Rear centre occupant without the second pretensioning stage
Safety note: pyrotechnic belt hardware; de-energise the system (battery off, wait time) and have a specialist workshop do the work
c: Plug at the rear centre buckle or anchor tensioner loosened by folding the bench
Airbag module coded for a rear centre B stage that is not present
Harness under the rear bench chafed or pinched

B007E.d: B007E is the driver's third (C) pretensioner circuit. Mercedes-Benz fills this slot with the retractor: in LI54.21-P-070658 for the A-, CLA- and GLB-Class, B007E13 is an open circuit at the squib of the driver's emergency tensioning retractor, with B0079 for the belt end fitting tensioner and B0080 for the driver's belt force limiter.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Driver's shoulder belt is not tightened in a crash
Safety note: the retractor holds a pyrotechnic charge; disconnect the battery, wait, and leave the work to a specialist workshop
c: Retractor plug at the lower driver-side B-pillar loose or terminals spread
Harness pinched by B-pillar or sill trim
Internal fault of the driver retractor pretensioner

B007F.d: B007F covers the passenger's third (C) pretensioner and is the best-documented code of this series. Mercedes lists B007F13 as an open in the squib of the front passenger's emergency tensioning retractor (A-, CLA- and GLB-Class).
s: Airbag warning lamp on, often after recent interior or body repair
Passenger shoulder belt not tightened in a crash
Safety note: pyrotechnic retractor in the B-pillar; work on it only de-energised (battery off, wait time) and at a specialist workshop
c: Retractor plug at the lower passenger-side B-pillar loose or with spread terminals (FCA S2008000193)
Body harness pinched between B-pillar trim retainer and body (FCA S2008000137)
Internal fault of the passenger retractor pretensioner

B0080.d: B0080 reports a fault in the firing loop that switches the driver's belt force limiter. In adaptive retractors a small squib, fired by the airbag module, changes the level at which the webbing is paid out, so the chest load suits crash severity and occupant.
s: Airbag warning lamp on, sometimes with an SRS message in the cluster
Driver's belt keeps only its basic force limiting level in a crash
Safety note: pyrotechnic part in the driver's retractor; work only de-energised (battery off, wait time) at a specialist workshop
c: Raised contact resistance at the airbag module connector (Mercedes LI54.21-P-070658)
Chafed or disconnected lead to the driver's retractor at the B-pillar
Restraint module software needing an update (Ford Fusion/MKZ)
Internal fault of the load limiter squib in the retractor

B0081.d: B0081 is assigned to a squib-switched limiter for the centre place of a three-across front bench. No carmaker publishes the code with this meaning.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
On GM vehicles the passenger airbag status shows OFF although an adult is seated
Safety note: airbag system with pyrotechnic parts; diagnose and repair only de-energised at a specialist workshop
c: On GM vehicles, fault or mismatch of the passenger presence module in the seat (different meaning)
Wiring to a centre front seat retractor damaged in the seat base
Internal fault of the centre seat load limiter squib

B0082.d: B0082 covers the firing loop of the front passenger's switchable belt force limiter. Two manufacturers document this meaning.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Passenger belt cannot switch its force limiting level in a crash
Safety note: pyrotechnic retractor at the passenger B-pillar; work only de-energised (battery off, wait time) at a specialist workshop
c: Poor connection at the passenger retractor plug (Ford C303B, SSM 51998)
Raised resistance at the airbag module connector (Mercedes LI54.21-P-070658)
Internal fault of the passenger retractor and limiter assembly

B0083.d: B0083 is intended for a switchable force limiter on the left rear seat. No manufacturer publishes it with this J2012 meaning.
s: Airbag warning lamp on, possibly only intermittently
Left rear belt keeps a fixed limiting level in a crash
Safety note: restraint system with pyrotechnic parts; work only de-energised at a specialist workshop
c: On GM vehicles, corroded left front impact sensor or unlatched connector lock (PI1480, different meaning)
Wiring to the left rear retractor damaged under trim or seat
Internal fault of the rear load limiter squib

B0084.d: B0084 names a squib-switched force limiter for the middle rear seat. Neither a carmaker nor a bulletin shows it with that meaning, and the hardware is rare: NHTSA's 2013 evaluation reports load limiters as standard only at the outer front seats, and the rear centre belt is often a plain retractor.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
On Saab 9-3/9-5 the second stage of the driver airbag is disabled
Safety note: airbag system with pyrotechnic parts; diagnose only de-energised at a specialist workshop
c: On GM vehicles, fault at the right front impact sensor or its plug (different meaning)
On Saab 9-3/9-5, open or short in the driver seat position sensor circuit (different meaning)
Damaged lead to a centre rear limiter where one is fitted

B0085.d: B0085 points to the igniter circuit that would change the force level of the right rear belt. No maker documents it with that meaning.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
On GM vehicles the code clears from history only after 100 fault-free ignition cycles
Safety note: pyrotechnic restraint parts; work only de-energised at a specialist workshop
c: On GM vehicles, left front side impact sensor or its door wiring faulty (different meaning)
Lead to the right rear retractor pinched by seat or trim
Internal fault of the right rear limiter squib

B0086.d: B0086 is reserved for a switchable force limiter at the left third-row seat. No manufacturer documents it, and an electrically fired limiter that far back is unusual.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Left third-row belt limits force only at a fixed level
Safety note: restraint system with pyrotechnic parts; work only de-energised at a specialist workshop
c: On GM vehicles, right front side impact sensor or wiring faulty (different meaning)
Third-row harness stressed by folding or removing the seat
Internal fault of the third-row limiter squib

B0087.d: B0087 would flag the igniter circuit of an adaptive belt force limiter on the centre position of row three. That combination is close to theoretical: no carmaker documents the code, and NHTSA's 2013 study dates universal fitment of load limiters (by model year 2007) only for the front outboard seats.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
On GM vehicles the AIR BAG indicator is lit by the cluster at the module's request
Safety note: airbag system with pyrotechnic parts; diagnose only de-energised at a specialist workshop
c: On GM vehicles, left rear side impact sensor or its connector faulty (different meaning)
Damaged lead to a third-row centre limiter where fitted

B0088.d: B0088 closes the load limiter series with the right third-row seat. No manufacturer documents it with this meaning.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Right third-row belt cannot change its limiting level
Safety note: pyrotechnic restraint parts; work only de-energised at a specialist workshop
c: On GM vehicles, right rear side impact sensor or wiring faulty (different meaning)
Harness to the right third-row seat strained by seat folding
Internal fault of the right third-row limiter squib

B0090.d: B0090 concerns the left frontal crash sensor, a satellite accelerometer in the front crumple zone that tells the airbag module early how hard the front end is being hit. Bosch notes such upfront units sharpen frontal crash detection beside the central sensors.
s: Airbag warning lamp on, often after front-end repair or water exposure
Frontal crash detection relies on the module's internal sensor only
Safety note: airbag system; disconnect the battery and observe the wait time before touching sensors or wiring, work at a specialist workshop
c: Water in the left front sensor connector damaging the harness (Acura 18-016)
Replacement sensor part number not matching the restraint controller (FCA S2408000050)
Restraint controller software needing a reflash (FCA TSB 08-150-26)
Sensor damaged by a front-end impact or poor refitting after body repair

B0091.d: B0091 covers the first left-side crash sensor, which Mitsubishi places in the front door and lists as DOOR SATEL SENS LH with the J2012 title in brackets. The airbag unit checks it with the ignition on and stores a subtype after a two-second delay: -11 for a short to ground, -55 when the configuration held in the unit does not fit the vehicle, -81 for a communication fault, plus further bytes.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Side and curtain airbags on the left may deploy late or not in a side impact
Safety note: airbag system; disconnect the battery and keep the wait time before door work, then have it checked at a specialist workshop
c: Short or poor contact in the door harness or connector to the sensor
Internal fault of the front door satellite sensor
Airbag unit configuration not matching the vehicle (Mitsubishi subtype -55)
Internal fault of the airbag diagnosis unit

B0092.d: B0092 belongs to the second crash sensor on the left side. Mitsubishi fits it at the left B-pillar and lists it as B-PILLAR SAT SEN LH, adding the J2012 title Left Side Restraints Sensor 2; its index shows only subtype -55, set two seconds after the unit finds that its stored configuration does not fit the vehicle.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Left side impact detection rests on the remaining sensors only
Safety note: airbag system; disconnect the battery and keep the wait time before removing pillar trim, work at a specialist workshop
c: Airbag unit configuration not matching the fitted sensors (Mitsubishi subtype -55)
Loose or corroded plug at the B-pillar sensor after trim or body work
On GM-built Saabs, passenger presence system fault (different meaning)
Internal fault of the B-pillar satellite sensor

B0093.d: B0093 is the third left-side crash sensor. Mitsubishi mounts it at the left C-pillar, names it C-PILLAR SAT SEN LH and gives the J2012 wording Left Side Restraints Sensor 3.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Left side impact sensing behind the front door is degraded
Safety note: airbag system; disconnect the battery and keep the wait time before work at the rear pillar, specialist workshop only
c: Sensor line shorted to ground or poor contact at the C-pillar plug (subtypes -11/-81)
Internal fault of the C-pillar satellite sensor
Airbag unit configuration not matching the vehicle (subtype -55)
Internal fault of the airbag diagnosis unit

B0094.d: B0094 refers to a single crash sensor placed in the middle of the vehicle front, used where a car has one central frontal satellite rather than a left and right pair. Mitsubishi's airbag unit shows it as CRASH ZONE SENS and adds the J2012 name Center Frontal Restraints Sensor.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Frontal crash detection falls back on the sensors inside the airbag unit
Safety note: airbag system; disconnect the battery and keep the wait time before work at the front sensor, specialist workshop only
c: Open, short or corroded contact in the harness to the centre front sensor (subtypes -11/-12/-88)
Internal fault of the crash zone sensor, e.g. offset or self-diagnosis error (subtypes -25/-28)
Sensor or airbag unit not the specified part, or unit configuration wrong (subtypes -86/-55)
Sensor or bracket bent by a front-end impact or refitted poorly after body work

B0095.d: B0095 is the right-hand partner of B0090: an acceleration satellite in the right front crumple zone that lets the airbag module judge early how severe a frontal hit is. Honda's Fit and HR-V of model years 2016–2017 use the code this way, B0095-87 meaning the right front impact sensor sends nothing; in request AER17060A Honda asked dealers to report such cars before any repair.
s: Airbag warning lamp on, often after front-end repair
Frontal impacts on the right are judged later or less precisely
Safety note: airbag system; disconnect the battery and keep the wait time before touching the sensor, specialist workshop only
c: Replacement sensor part number not matching the restraint controller (FCA S2408000050)
Water or road salt in the sensor housing or plug at the right front
Restraint controller software needing a reflash (FCA TSB 08-150-26)
Internal failure of the right front acceleration sensor

B0096.d: B0096 concerns the first crash sensor on the right side, mirror image of B0091. Mitsubishi puts it in the right front door, calls it DOOR SATEL SENS RH and prints the J2012 title beside it; its airbag unit checks the sensor with the ignition on and, after two seconds, stores -11 for a ground short, -81 when data from the sensor stop and -55 for a configuration that does not fit the car, among nine subtypes in total.
s: Airbag warning lamp on, sometimes only after the right front door has been opened or worked on
Side and curtain airbags on the right may fire late in a side impact
Safety note: airbag system; disconnect the battery and keep the wait time before removing the door trim, specialist workshop only
c: Chafed wire or poor contact in the door harness between body and right front door
Internal fault of the right front door satellite sensor
Airbag unit configuration not matching the vehicle (Mitsubishi subtype -55)
On Saab 9-3/9-5, passenger belt buckle switch circuit fault (different meaning)

B0097.d: B0097 is the second right-side crash sensor. Mitsubishi fixes it at the right B-pillar, lists it as B-PILLAR SAT SEN RH and gives Right Side Restraints Sensor 2 as the J2012 name.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Right side impacts near the B-pillar are detected only by the remaining sensors
Safety note: airbag system; disconnect the battery and keep the wait time before removing pillar trim, specialist workshop only
c: Airbag unit configuration not matching the fitted sensors, e.g. after unit replacement (Mitsubishi subtype -55)
Plug at the right B-pillar sensor loose or damaged after trim or seat belt work
Right B-pillar sensor sending no signal (Honda subtype -87)
On Saab 9-3/9-5, driver belt buckle switch circuit fault (different meaning)

B0098.d: B0098 belongs to the third right-side crash sensor. In Mitsubishi's airbag index it is the C-PILLAR SAT SEN RH, given with the J2012 wording Right Side Restraints Sensor 3.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Right side impact sensing at the rear door is degraded
Safety note: airbag system; disconnect the battery and keep the wait time before work at the rear pillar, specialist workshop only
c: Open or shorted line or poor contact at the right C-pillar plug (subtypes -11/-12/-88/-81)
Internal fault of the right C-pillar sensor, e.g. offset or reset error (subtypes -28/-93)
Airbag unit configuration not matching the vehicle (subtype -55)
On the Saab 9-3, passenger presence system fault (different meaning)

B0099.d: B0099 reports a fault in the rollover sensing that decides whether curtain airbags and pretensioners fire when a vehicle tips. Bosch integrates rollover sensors in its base airbag control unit, so the sensor is often part of the module.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Curtain airbags and pretensioners may not fire in a rollover
Safety note: airbag control unit with rollover sensing; work only de-energised (battery off, wait time) at a specialist workshop
c: Internal fault of the rollover sensor built into the airbag control unit (module replacement)
Airbag unit loose, mounted at an angle or after a crash no longer within its fitting tolerance
Wiring or plug fault where a separate rollover sensor is fitted
Restraint controller software or configuration not matching the vehicle

B009A.d: B009A extends the left-side sensor row past the three positions most cars use. No carmaker documents this code publicly.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Left side impact detection in the area of the missing sensor is weaker
Safety note: airbag system; disconnect the battery and keep the wait time before any work on sensors or wiring, specialist workshop only
c: Damaged line or plug to the fourth left sensor, often after seat or trim removal
Internal fault of the fourth left crash satellite
Airbag module coded for a sensor layout the vehicle does not have

B009B.d: B009B names a fifth crash sensor on the left side. No carmaker documents this code publicly, and the reviewed bulletins and airbag indexes stop well before it.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Side and curtain airbags on the left may deploy later in a side impact
Safety note: airbag system; switch off, disconnect the battery and keep the wait time before work, specialist workshop only
c: Line or connector fault on the way to the fifth left sensor
Internal fault of the fifth left satellite (pressure or acceleration type)
Replacement sensor of the wrong part number after a body repair

B009C.d: B009C is the sixth and last left-side slot in the J2012 sensor block. No carmaker documents this code publicly.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Side impact sensing at the rear left is reduced
Safety note: airbag system; disconnect the battery and keep the wait time, then have it diagnosed at a specialist workshop
c: Airbag module configured for more side sensors than are fitted
Damaged rear body harness or plug to the sixth left sensor
Internal fault of the sixth left satellite

B009D.d: B009D opens the second half of the right-side sensor row, after B0096 to B0098. No carmaker documents this code publicly; Mitsubishi stops its right row at the C-pillar sensor B0098, and Honda's Fit and HR-V use only two side sensors per side.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Right side impact detection in the area of that sensor is weaker
Safety note: airbag system; disconnect the battery and keep the wait time before work on sensors, specialist workshop only
c: Communication with the fourth right sensor lost through wiring, plug or sensor fault
Internal fault of the fourth right crash satellite
Airbag module coded for a sensor layout the vehicle does not have

B009E.d: B009E stands for a fifth crash sensor on the vehicle's right flank. No carmaker documents this code publicly: Mitsubishi's airbag index ends its right row with the C-pillar unit B0098, and the NHTSA bulletin index shows no entry for B009E at all.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Side and curtain airbags on the right may react later in the area of that sensor
Safety note: airbag system; unplug sensors only with the ignition off, battery disconnected and wait time observed; after replacement have the configuration checked, specialist workshop only
c: Open, shorted or corroded line or plug to the fifth right sensor, often after door or trim work
Internal fault of the fifth right crash sensor (pressure or acceleration type)
Airbag control unit coded for a sensor that the vehicle does not have

B009F.d: B009F would be the sixth and last right-hand restraints sensor in the J2012 block. No carmaker documents it publicly with this meaning.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
On GM two-mode hybrids, no crank or a Service Hybrid message instead
Safety note: airbag and, on hybrids, high-voltage system; disconnect plugs only de-energised; after a sensor change have it checked or initialised, specialist workshop only
c: Damaged rear body harness or plug to the sixth right sensor
Internal fault of the sixth right acceleration satellite
On GM two-mode hybrids, water or corrosion at the high-voltage impact detection sensor (different meaning, PIT4614C)

B00A0.d: B00A0 is the catch-all code for occupant classification, the function that judges at the front passenger place whether the passenger airbag may fire and with what force, as FMVSS 208 demands for advanced airbags. Mitsubishi lists it as OCCUPANT SENS UNIT with ten subtypes, among them sensor faults (-02/-09), low supply or unfinished zero-point reset (-22, battery at 9 V or less), lost communication (-83/-86/-87/-88)
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Passenger airbag status lamp shows the wrong state or the passenger airbag stays switched off
Fault may appear only after cold starts with a weak battery
Safety note: airbag system; unplug seat and sensor connectors only de-energised; after replacing seat sensors or the unit, the zero-point reset/calibration must be done, specialist workshop only
c: Poor contact or open circuit in the passenger seat harness or plug, often after seat removal
Low battery voltage or voltage dip while cranking (Mitsubishi -22, Mazda B00A0:09)
Zero-point reset not done or not possible after seat work (Nissan reprograms the unit)
Internal fault of the classification sensor or control unit, often replaced with the seat cushion

B00A1.d: B00A1 covers the occupant position system, which watches where a person sits rather than how heavy they are, so that an airbag can be held back when someone is too close to it. FMVSS 208 accepts this as dynamic automatic suppression (DASS): the bag must be switched off before the occupant's head, neck or upper body reach a zone beside the cover that the maker defines.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Airbag off indicator stays on although the occupant sits upright
Safety note: airbag system; disconnect seat and sensor plugs only de-energised; after a sensor or unit change initialise/calibrate the system, specialist workshop only
c: System not initialised after seat cover, seat-back sensor or control unit replacement
Damaged seat harness or loose plug under the seat
Faulty position sensor or position control unit
Damp seat, accessory seat covers or objects disturbing the sensors

B00B0.d: B00B0 is the first of five classification inputs on the driver seat. No carmaker publishes this code, and J2012 leaves it to the maker which sensor the letter A means.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Driver airbag may deploy with a fixed instead of an adapted stage
Safety note: airbag system; unplug seat and sensor connectors only de-energised (ignition off, battery off, wait time); calibrate the sensor after replacement, specialist workshop only
c: Open or poor contact in the driver seat harness or plug to input A
Cushion sensor mat creased or damaged, e.g. after seat cover work
Sensor or seat replaced without the required zero-point calibration

B00B1.d: B00B1 marks the second of the five driver seat classification sensors. No carmaker documents it publicly, and the letter is not tied to a fixed spot.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Weight-based adjustment of the driver airbag unavailable
Safety note: airbag system; work on seat and sensor plugs only de-energised; calibrate the seat sensors after replacement or seat refitting, specialist workshop only
c: Seat refitted with wrong bolt torque or distorted mounting, loading the sensor unevenly
Strained or chafed lead to load input B under the seat
Internal fault of the strain gauge sensor

B00B2.d: B00B2 is the third driver seat classification sensor in the J2012 list. No carmaker documents the code publicly.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Driver airbag cannot be matched to occupant size
Safety note: airbag system; disconnect seat and sensor plugs only de-energised (ignition off, battery off, wait time); calibrate weight sensors after replacement, specialist workshop only
c: Internal fault of the Hall-type sensor bolt at seat anchor C
Sensor bolt overloaded or seat frame bent, e.g. after a crash or wrong torque
Open or poor contact in the lead to input C

B00B3.d: B00B3 refers to the fourth of five driver seat classification inputs. No carmaker publishes it, and the mapping of letters to sensors is undocumented.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Classification of the driver unavailable for airbag staging
Safety note: airbag system; unplug seat and sensor connectors only de-energised (ignition off, battery off, wait time); recalibrate after any sensor change, specialist workshop only
