c: Seat harness worn by seat movement, open or intermittent contact to input D
Sensor binding or preloaded in the seat structure
Recalibration not done after sensor or unit replacement
Internal fault of the sensor, e.g. leaking bladder or failed pressure cell

B00B4.d: B00B4 is the fifth and last driver seat classification sensor. No carmaker documents the code publicly.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Possible related faults of the seat heater on the same seat
Safety note: airbag system; work on seat and sensor plugs only de-energised; after replacing a sensor or trim follow the maker's calibration, specialist workshop only
c: Open or poor contact in the seat harness or plug to input E
Damaged seat heater or trim where the capacitive electrode shares its layer
Internal fault of the fifth classification sensor or its electronics

B00B5.d: B00B5 reports a fault of the driver seat track position sensor, which tells the airbag module whether the seat is pushed far forward toward the steering wheel. FCA uses it with exactly this meaning: GPOP tech tips for the Dodge Dart (PF), Jeep Cherokee (KL) and Chrysler 200 (UF) name B00B5-13, an open circuit, among codes to clear with engineering before replacing the restraint controller, and a 2024 tip for the Paci
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Driver airbag may fire without seat position adjustment (e.g. second stage locked out)
Safety note: airbag system; unplug the seat and sensor connectors only de-energised; after replacing the sensor check its position output/calibration, specialist workshop only
c: Open circuit or bent/corroded pins in the seat harness to the track sensor (FCA subtype -13)
Sensor loose or wrongly positioned on the seat track, so the Hall switch no longer sees the track edge
Low system voltage (FCA asks to check this before replacing the controller)
Internal fault of the Hall-effect seat track sensor

B00B6.d: B00B6 concerns a sensor that tells the restraint system how far the backrest of the driver seat is reclined. No carmaker documents this code publicly, and the NHTSA bulletin index has no entry for it.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Airbag adaptation to a reclined seating position unavailable
Safety note: airbag system; disconnect seat and sensor plugs only de-energised (ignition off, battery off, wait time); calibrate the sensor after replacement, specialist workshop only
c: Lead pinched or broken at the seat back hinge, where it flexes with every adjustment
Internal fault or loose mounting of the recline sensor
Sensor or seat back replaced without the required zero setting

B00B7.d: B00B7 is the first of five occupant position sensors for the driver seat. No carmaker publishes the code, and J2012 does not say which sensor the letter A means.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Out-of-position suppression of the driver airbag unavailable

Safety note: airbag system; disconnect sensor and seat plugs only de-energised (ignition off, battery off, wait time); calibrate/initialise position sensors after replacement, specialist workshop only
c: Open or poor contact in the lead to position sensor A (e.g. headliner or trim harness)
Sensor face covered, dirty or misaligned after trim work
Internal fault of position sensor A

B00B8.d: B00B8 names the second occupant position sensor at the driver seat. The code is not published by any carmaker, and the letter assignment is the maker's choice.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Airbag cannot be suppressed if the driver is very close to the cover
Safety note: airbag system; work at steering wheel, cover or sensor plugs only de-energised (ignition off, battery off, wait time); calibrate the sensor after replacement, specialist workshop only
c: Fault in the lead to a sensor at the steering wheel or cover, e.g. via the clockspring
Sensor window covered by stickers, covers or dirt
Internal fault of position sensor B

B00B9.d: B00B9 is the third occupant position sensor of the driver seat. No carmaker publishes it.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Side airbag suppression for leaning occupants unavailable
Safety note: airbag system with seat side airbag; disconnect seat plugs only de-energised; initialise/calibrate after sensor or cover replacement, specialist workshop only
c: Seat-back cover or sensor replaced without initialisation
Damaged seat-back harness or plug under the seat
Damp seat or accessory seat cover disturbing the electric field

B00BA.d: B00BA covers position input D, the fourth of the driver seat sensors. Its use by a carmaker is not documented publicly.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Staged driver airbag deployment based on position restricted
Safety note: airbag system; disconnect sensor and seat plugs only de-energised (ignition off, battery off, wait time); calibrate position sensors after replacement, specialist workshop only
c: Open or shorted lead to position sensor D
Signal disagreeing with the other position inputs, e.g. sensor dirty or misaligned
Internal fault of position sensor D

B00BB.d: B00BB is the fifth and last driver seat occupant position sensor in the J2012 block. No carmaker publishes this code.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Position-based adjustment of the driver airbag partly unavailable
Safety note: airbag system; disconnect sensor and seat plugs only de-energised (ignition off, battery off, wait time); calibrate the sensor after replacement, specialist workshop only
c: Open, shorted or loose lead to position sensor E
Restraint module configured for a fifth position sensor that is not fitted
Internal fault of position sensor E

B00C0.d: B00C0 flags the first of up to five classification inputs in the front passenger seat. Their job comes from FMVSS 208: the passenger bag must stay off when a 12-month dummy sits in a listed child restraint or a newborn dummy lies in a car bed, yet it must be live for a 5th percentile woman, and a yellow PASSENGER AIR BAG OFF lamp reports the suppressed state.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Passenger airbag off lamp shows a state that does not match the occupant
Safety note: passenger airbag may be wrongly enabled or disabled; seat and sensor plugs only de-energised, recalibrate the classification after repairs, specialist workshop only
c: Loose plug or chafed wire to input A under the passenger seat, often after the seat was removed
Classification sensor A itself delivers no or an implausible signal
Objects under the seat, items hanging on the seat back or pressure from the rear disturbing the measurement

B00C1.d: B00C1 belongs to input B of the passenger seat classification. It is unpublished as such, but Toyota shows why a seat can carry several such sensors: on 2012–2013 Camry, Prius c and Yaris and 2013 Avalon, a left and a right weight detector sit between seat frame and rails.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Passenger airbag off lamp lit although an adult is seated
Safety note: passenger airbag status may be wrong; disconnect seat sensors only de-energised, keep tightening torques and run the zero-point calibration with the scan tool, specialist workshop only
c: Load cell B damaged or drifting, for example after the seat was forced or dropped
Seat pan or sensor bolts fitted under tension or with the wrong torque, preloading the cell
Zero-point calibration not done after sensor or seat work
Poor contact at the plug of sensor B

B00C2.d: B00C2 names the third classification input of the passenger seat. No carmaker documents it, and nobody has tied the letter to a known part.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Fault may come and go with weather or after cleaning the seat
Safety note: a child on the passenger seat may not be detected; replace mats only as the maker's kit with the seat de-energised, then recalibrate, specialist workshop only
c: Liquid, rain or condensation soaked into the seat cushion and sensor
Sensor mat cracked or worn from years of getting in and out
Damaged lead or plug between mat and classification unit

B00C3.d: B00C3 is the fourth passenger seat classification input. No carmaker documents it under this number.
s: Airbag warning lamp or airbag symbol on the display
Fault may depend on seat position or on other electrical loads being switched on
Safety note: occupant classification unreliable; work on seat wiring only de-energised (12 V off, wait time), use the maker's filter or rework kit where one exists, specialist workshop only
c: Electrical interference coupled into the seat harness (seat heating, motors, routing near other leads)
Harness under tension or plug loose at the classification module when the seat moves
Internal fault of sensor D or the classification module

B00C4.d: B00C4 stands for the fifth and last passenger seat classification input; no public carmaker source uses it. Two field cases show what goes wrong besides wiring.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Passenger belt warning or airbag status lamp does not match who or what is on the seat
Safety note: passenger airbag may stay enabled for a child seat; disconnect only de-energised, calibrate with the maker's procedure after any module change, specialist workshop only
c: Classification module calibrated wrongly or not at all after replacement
Open or high-resistance contact on the lead to input E
Electronic devices or other objects on the seat confusing the sensing

B00C5.d: B00C5 reports a fault of the sensor that tells the restraint controller where the passenger seat sits on its rails. FCA uses the code with exactly this name.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Passenger airbag deployment can no longer be adapted to the seat position

Safety note: airbag system; disconnect under-seat plugs only de-energised (ignition off, battery off, wait time), do not replace the restraint controller before checking pins, specialist workshop only
c: Terminal pushed back or loose in the under-seat connector (FCA Durango, R730 return wire)
Lead to the track sensor pinched or torn by the moving seat
Track position sensor faulty or its gap to the rail wrong after seat work
Restraint controller internal fault, only after wiring and sensor are ruled out

B00C6.d: B00C6 concerns the sensor that reports how far the passenger seat back is reclined. It appears neither in any public carmaker list nor in NHTSA bulletins.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Passenger airbag off lamp may light for an adult sitting with the seat back reclined
Safety note: airbag system; work on seat back and sensor only de-energised (ignition off, battery off, wait time), relearn or calibrate afterwards, specialist workshop only
c: Lead to the recline sensor stretched or broken at the seat back hinge
Recline potentiometer or inclination sensor worn or faulty
Angle reference not learned after replacing the seat back or the sensor

B00C7.d: B00C7 opens the row of five passenger seat position sensors, a code absent from all public carmaker documents. The passenger seat is where position sensing reached series cars: Honda's OPDS puts sensors in the passenger seat back that judge sitting height and whether a child leans toward the door, and then blocks the seat-mounted side airbag and lights a side airbag off indicator.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Side airbag off indicator lit although the passenger sits upright
Safety note: side airbag may be wrongly enabled or blocked; work on the seat back only de-energised and initialise the system afterwards, specialist workshop only
c: Position system not initialised after seat cover, seat back sensor or control unit replacement
Electrode or lead in the seat back damaged, for instance by a non-original seat cover or repairs
Damp seat back or objects pressed against it

B00C8.d: B00C8 marks the second occupant position sensor of the passenger seat. No carmaker publishes it.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Passenger airbag may be suppressed or released without regard to sitting position
Safety note: airbag system; disconnect seat sensors only de-energised (ignition off, battery off, wait time), recalibrate after work on the seat, specialist workshop only
c: Plug or lead to sensor B damaged when the seat was moved or removed
Strain gauge bridge or position sensor B faulty, drifting with temperature
Seat frame mounted under tension, so the load split looks implausible

B00C9.d: B00C9 names position sensor C of the passenger seat, and no carmaker lists it publicly. One concept for a third input watches the gap between torso and seat back: a patent first filed by Automotive Systems Laboratory in 1998, now with Joyson, pairs an electric field sensor in the cushion with a capacitive or radar proximity sensor in the back, aimed at the band about 10 to 18 inches above the cushion.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Airbag status lamp may change while the passenger leans forward
Safety note: airbag system; seat back and sensor only de-energised (ignition off, battery off, wait time), no third-party seat covers over sensors, specialist workshop only
c: Lead to the seat back sensor broken at the hinge or after trim work
Proximity sensor C faulty or its signal disagrees with the cushion sensor
Thick accessory covers or a wet seat back weakening the field signal

B00CA.d: B00CA is position input D, the fourth for the passenger seat. Its use is not documented by any carmaker.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Out-of-position suppression for the passenger no longer available
Safety note: airbag system; work at pillar, headliner or dashboard only de-energised (ignition off, battery off, wait time), recheck sensor alignment afterwards, specialist workshop only
c: Lead to sensor D damaged at the pillar, headliner or dashboard after trim or glass work
Sensor view blocked or lens dirty, for example by stickers or accessories
Internal fault of position sensor D

B00CB.d: B00CB is the fifth and last passenger seat occupant position sensor. No carmaker publishes it.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Passenger airbag deploys without position-based suppression or staging
Safety note: airbag system; disconnect sensors only de-energised (ignition off, battery off, wait time), check configuration after replacement, specialist workshop only
c: Open or shorted lead to sensor E in the headliner, mirror base or dashboard
Transducer of sensor E faulty or covered
Restraint module coded for a sensor the vehicle does not carry

B00D0.d: B00D0 reports a fault in the driver's seat belt warning, meaning the lamp, its circuit or the output or message that drives it, not the buckle switch. No carmaker documents it publicly.
s: Driver belt warning lamp stays dark or stays on regardless of the belt
Airbag or restraint warning lamp may be on
Safety note: legally required warning missing; buckle up regardless, cluster and restraint wiring only de-energised (ignition off, battery off, wait time), specialist workshop
c: Open or shorted lamp circuit or connector between restraint module and cluster
Warning lamp or LED in the instrument cluster failed
Belt warning message not received by the cluster, for example after a cluster change without configuration

B00D1.d: B00D1 covers the passenger seat belt warning. Unlike the driver warning, it only makes sense if the car knows the seat is occupied, so it leans on occupant sensing.
s: No passenger belt reminder, or a reminder for an empty seat
Airbag or restraint warning lamp may be on
Safety note: passenger may ride unbelted without warning; wiring work only de-energised (ignition off, battery off, wait time), specialist workshop
c: Open or shorted circuit to the passenger belt lamp or its display segment
Lamp, LED or display unit for the passenger warning failed
Occupancy information missing or wrong, so the warning logic cannot run

B00D2.d: B00D2 means the restraint module has found a fault in the circuit of its primary warning lamp, the airbag or SRS light. FMVSS 208 S4.5.2 requires such a readiness indicator, watching its own readiness and within the driver's view, and FMVSS 101 lets it push other messages out of a shared display.
s: Airbag lamp does not come on for the bulb check at ignition-on, or stays on
A substitute warning such as a central warning lamp or a tone may appear
Safety note: airbag faults may go unnoticed; work on cluster and restraint wiring only de-energised (ignition off, battery off, wait time), specialist workshop only
c: Bulb or LED of the airbag warning lamp failed
Lamp lead open, shorted to ground or to battery voltage, or loose cluster connector
Internal fault in the instrument cluster circuit board

B00D3.d: B00D3 refers to a second restraint malfunction indicator. No carmaker documents which lamp that is, so its meaning has to be inferred.
s: Airbag lamp on, second indicator dark or not doing its bulb check
Backup warning missing if the main airbag lamp also fails
Safety note: restraint warnings incomplete; work on cluster and wiring only de-energised (ignition off, battery off, wait time), specialist workshop only
c: Open or shorted circuit to the second restraint indicator
Second indicator lamp or LED failed
Restraint module or cluster configured for an indicator the vehicle does not have

B00D4.d: B00D4 concerns the audible restraint warning, the tone that stands in when a fault cannot be shown by the lamp. Ford's 2014 F-150 manual describes it: system readiness is signalled by the warning light, or by a backup tone if the light is out, and a problem announces itself as five beeps in a row, repeated until the fault and the lamp are put right.
s: No warning tone where one would be expected, other warning chimes may also be silent
Airbag warning lamp on
Safety note: fallback warning missing; work on cluster and restraint wiring only de-energised (ignition off, battery off, wait time), specialist workshop
c: Open or shorted lead to the chime or speaker used for restraint warnings
Chime module or cluster speaker failed
Tone request from the restraint module not received by the sounding unit

B00D5.d: B00D5 concerns the lamp that tells the front occupants the passenger airbag is off. FMVSS 208 wants it yellow, worded PASSENGER AIR BAG OFF (short form PASS AIR BAG OFF) and separate from the readiness lamp; Ford's 2014 F-150 places it by the radio and lights it briefly at start as a self-test.
s: Passenger airbag off lamp stays dark during the start check or shows the wrong state
Airbag warning lamp on
Safety note: occupants cannot see whether the passenger airbag is off; do not fit a rear-facing child seat until repaired, wiring only de-energised, specialist workshop
c: Indicator lead shorted to ground, shorted to power or open (Mitsubishi -11/-12/-13)
Passenger airbag off indicator itself failed
Network or gateway software fault, as on 2021 Ford Edge/Nautilus (SSM 50127)
Internal fault of the airbag control unit output

B00DF.d: B00DF is set for the key switch that lets the passenger airbag be turned off by hand. FMVSS 208 S4.5.4 allowed it on vehicles built before September 2012 with no forward rear seats or a short rear row; it must take the key, stay apart from the ignition and keep the bag off until switched back, and 49 CFR 595.5 governs retrofits under an NHTSA letter.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Passenger airbag does not follow the switch position, or the off lamp disagrees with it
Safety note: passenger airbag state uncertain; no rear-facing child seat on that seat until checked, wiring and switch only de-energised (ignition off, battery off, wait time), specialist workshop
c: Switch circuits present in the harness of a vehicle without the switch, damaged or picking up faults (FCA B00DF-95)
Key switch worn or its lead open or shorted
Restraint module software counter or configuration error (Ford B00DF:4A)

B00E0.d: B00E0 points to a second pretensioner stage (B) on the left seat of the third row. Such a stage would be an extra device next to the retractor, typically a lap or anchor tensioner that pulls on the lower belt end.
s: Airbag warning lamp lit
Lap belt at the left third-row seat may not be pulled tight in a crash
Safety note: pyrotechnic part – work only with the battery disconnected and the wait time observed, preferably at a specialist workshop
c: Plug of the lap or anchor tensioner at the left third-row seat loose, unlatched or corroded
Lead strained or chafed by folding and stowing the third-row seat
Airbag module coded for a B stage the vehicle does not have (after module or seat replacement)
Internal open or short in the tensioner squib

B00E1.d: On the right seat of the third row, B00E1 stands for a B-stage tensioner whose firing loop shows an open, a short or an out-of-window resistance. In no public service document does a manufacturer use B00E1.
s: Airbag lamp on in the instrument cluster
Occupant at the right of the third row gets no B-stage tensioning
Safety note: the tensioner contains a pyrotechnic charge; only work on it de-energised (battery off, wait time) and leave it to a specialist workshop
c: Connector of the right third-row buckle or anchor tensioner not fully seated
Wiring under the cargo floor or side trim pinched or damaged by loads
Raised contact resistance at the airbag module plug

B00E2.d: B00E2 would report the firing circuit of a B-stage tensioner at the centre seat of the third row. This is about the rarest slot in the pretensioner table: a centre seat in row three is uncommon, and a second tensioner stage on it even more so.
s: Airbag indicator stays on after the self-test
Centre occupant of the third row may lack lap-belt tensioning in a crash
Safety note: pyrotechnic restraint component – disconnect the battery, wait the specified time and have the work done by a specialist
c: Module variant coding expects a centre B stage that is not installed
Plug under the third-row centre seat disconnected after seat removal
Squib of the centre lap tensioner open or shorted internally

B00E3.d: B00E3 is the C-stage tensioner of the left outer rear seat, and two makers document it codegenau. Stellantis case S2408000089 (Jeep Wrangler 2023) has the occupant restraint controller store B00E3-13, named there for the retractor tensioner at the left of row two, after a service visit; the fix was to secure connector D3244A with a push-pull-push check, no parts.
s: Airbag warning lamp or SRS message in the cluster
Left rear shoulder belt is not retracted in a crash
Safety note: the retractor pretensioner is pyrotechnic; work only with the system de-energised (battery off, wait time) and preferably at a specialist workshop
c: Retractor pretensioner plug not latched after trim or seat work (Jeep Wrangler 2023, connector D3244A)
High contact resistance at the airbag control unit connector (Mercedes LI54.21-P-070658)
Lead to the left rear retractor chafed at the C-pillar or seat frame
Faulty squib in the retractor pretensioner

B00E4.d: B00E4 belongs to the outboard seat on the right in the back and its C-stage tensioner. Mercedes-Benz uses it in that sense: every version of LI54.21-P-070658 seen here (December 2019 to June 2020) lists B00E413 as an open in the squib of the tensioning retractor at the rear right.
s: SRS message or airbag lamp permanently displayed
Right rear passenger loses shoulder-belt tensioning
Safety note: pyrotechnic tensioner – only work on it with the battery disconnected and after the wait time, ideally at a specialist workshop
c: Poor contact at the SRS control unit plug (Mercedes A-Class/CLA/GLB)
Plug at the right rear retractor loose after trim removal
Airbag control unit itself faulty (fault returns after reconnecting)
Squib in the right rear retractor open

B00E5.d: B00E5 covers a C-stage tensioner at the middle seat of row two. No manufacturer publishes it.
s: Airbag lamp on
Rear centre passenger may not be held back early in a frontal crash
Safety note: the tensioner holds a pyrotechnic charge – battery off, wait time observed, repair at a specialist workshop
c: Centre-seat tensioner plug under the rear bench not engaged
Module coded for a centre tensioner that the vehicle lacks
Lead damaged where it passes the split or folding rear bench hinge

B00E6.d: Note the order in this block: B00E6 is the right seat of the third row, while B00E7 is the left. Mercedes-Benz fills B00E6 with the retractor tensioner on that seat: LI54.21-P-070658 (first issued December 2019 for A-Class and CLA, extended to GLB in version 4) reads B00E613 as an interrupted igniter in the tensioning retractor on the right of row three.
s: SRS message or airbag warning lamp
Right third-row belt stays slack in a crash
Safety note: work on this pyrotechnic retractor only de-energised (battery disconnected, wait time) and preferably by a specialist
c: Contact resistance at the airbag unit connector (Mercedes LI54.21-P-070658)
Plug of the right third-row retractor behind the cargo trim loose
Wiring in the rear wheel arch area pinched by trim or cargo
Squib of the right third-row retractor defective

B00E7.d: B00E7 marks the C-stage tensioner of the third row's left seat, listed after its right-hand twin B00E6. Mercedes-Benz documents it: LI54.21-P-070658 uses B00E713 when the firing pill of the left third-row tensioning retractor shows an open, in the same list as the rear and driver retractors.
s: Airbag lamp or fixed SRS message
No pretensioning for the left third-row seat
Safety note: pyrotechnic device – disconnect the battery and wait before touching it; have it serviced at a specialist workshop
c: Raised resistance at the restraint unit plug
Left third-row retractor connector disturbed during trim or seat work
Control unit below the required level, fault keeps returning

B00E8.d: B00E8 closes the C row of the table with the centre seat of the third row. No manufacturer publishes it, and the one public list that uses this block, Mercedes-Benz LI54.21-P-070658, stops at a left and a right third-row retractor (B00E7, B00E6).
s: Airbag warning lamp illuminated
Centre seat of the third row without belt tensioning
Safety note: contains a pyrotechnic charge – no work without disconnecting the battery and waiting; leave it to a specialist workshop
c: Connector of the seat-mounted centre retractor unplugged after removing the rear bench
Restraint module coded for a three-seat third row on a two-seat vehicle
Squib of the centre retractor faulty

B00F0.d: B00F0 is the firing circuit for an inflatable belt at the driver's seat: a section of webbing that a gas source fills in a crash so the load spreads over a wider area of the chest. The production inflatable belts known from Ford and Mercedes-Benz sit only at rear outer seats; no carmaker documents B00F0.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Driver belt would not inflate in a crash
Safety note: the belt contains a pyrotechnic gas generator; work only de-energised (battery off, wait time) and at a specialist workshop
c: Airbag module variant expects a driver inflatable belt that is not fitted
Plug of the belt gas generator at the lower anchor or seat loose or corroded
Lead to the inflator chafed by seat adjustment
Igniter of the belt inflator faulty

B00F1.d: B00F1 is the front passenger counterpart of B00F0, reserved for an inflatable belt at that seat. No manufacturer documents it, and no series vehicle is publicly known to have a passenger inflatable belt; Mercedes' S-Class manual offers the beltbag only for the outer rear belts.
s: Airbag lamp lit in the cluster
Passenger belt cannot inflate in a crash
Safety note: pyrotechnic belt inflator – disconnect the battery, respect the wait time and have repairs done by a specialist workshop
c: Module coded for a passenger inflatable belt that the car does not have
Connector at the buckle-side inflator under the passenger seat loose
Seat wiring damaged by objects under the seat or by seat movement

B00F2.d: B00F2 covers the inflatable belt at the left outer seat of row two, the position where such belts actually reached production. Ford offered them from the 2011 Explorer; its 2018 owner's manual puts the bag into the shoulder part of the belts at both outer seats in row two, filled with cooled gas at lower pressure, deployed in frontal, side and rollover crashes and monitored by the same module and lamp as the front be
s: Airbag warning light on
Left rear inflatable belt may not deploy in a crash
Safety note: the belt holds a stored-gas or pyrotechnic inflator – battery off, wait time, work only at a specialist workshop
c: Internal wire damage in the second-row seat harness at the belt connector (Ford programme 21B11)
Plug of the inflator under the left rear seat loose after folding or removing the seat
Fault in the belt inflator igniter

B00F3.d: B00F3 refers to an inflatable belt at the centre seat of the second row. No manufacturer documents the code, and the known systems leave this seat out: Ford's 2018 Explorer manual limits its inflatable belts to the outermost second-row positions, and Mercedes fits its beltbag to the outer rear belts (S-Class manual 2017); the E-Class manual of the same year lists the belt air bag as a frontal-impact device.
s: Airbag indicator remains on
Rear centre belt would not inflate in a crash
Safety note: pyrotechnic or stored-gas inflator – only work with the battery disconnected and the wait time observed, at a specialist workshop
c: Restraint module configured for a centre inflatable belt not present in the vehicle
Connector at the centre buckle inflator under the bench disconnected
Igniter of the centre belt inflator open or shorted

B00F4.d: B00F4 covers the inflatable belt on the outboard right seat of row two. The hardware exists in series cars, but the code is not documented by any maker.
s: Airbag lamp illuminated
Right rear inflatable belt not ready to deploy
Safety note: do not open or probe the belt or its inflator; battery off, wait time, and leave the job to a specialist workshop
c: Worn or broken wires in the right second-row seat pigtail (Ford Explorer 2014–2016)
Inflator plug at the lower belt anchor or under the seat not latched

B00F5.d: B00F5 opens the third-row part of the inflatable-belt block with the left seat; B00F6 (centre) and B00F7 (right) follow. No manufacturer documents B00F5, and the known systems stop at row two: Ford's Explorer has its inflatable belts only at the second-row outer seats, even though it has a third row, and Mercedes offers the beltbag for rear belts of S- and E-Class (outer seats in the S-Class).
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Left third-row inflatable belt not available in a crash
Safety note: inflator with explosive igniter – disconnect the battery, wait, and have it handled by a specialist workshop
c: Airbag module coded with a third-row inflatable belt that is not installed
Plug at the left third-row belt inflator disturbed when folding the seat
Defective igniter in the third-row belt inflator

B00F6.d: B00F6 names the deployment circuit for an inflatable belt at the middle seat of row three. That seat is the least likely place for such a belt: the series systems on record sit at outboard rear seats, Ford's Explorer only in row two and Mercedes' beltbag on the outer rear belts.
s: Airbag warning lamp lit
Centre third-row inflatable belt would not inflate in a crash
Safety note: igniter-equipped part – battery off, observe waiting time, work only in a specialist workshop
c: Airbag module coded for a centre third-row inflatable belt the vehicle does not have
Inflator plug of the centre belt loosened when the third-row seat was folded or removed
Igniter in the centre belt inflator out of its resistance window

B00F7.d: B00F7 closes the inflatable-belt block with the right seat of row three. No manufacturer documents it.
s: Airbag lamp stays on after start-up check
Right third-row inflatable belt not armed
Safety note: never probe the inflator circuit with a test lamp; disconnect battery, wait, leave it to a specialist
c: Chafed wires in the right rear seat harness, as seen one row forward on the Explorer (B141C)
Restraint module variant coding expects a right third-row inflatable belt
Open or shorted igniter in the right third-row belt inflator
